intro.title: Toggle Visibility
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an interactive component that can show or hide content when a user clicks a button. You'll learn how to use Angular's property binding and event handling to control element visibility dynamically. The core programming concept involves managing component state with boolean variables and using Angular's built-in directives like *ngIf or [hidden] to conditionally display elements. You'll work with TypeScript methods, click event handlers, and Angular's template syntax to create a responsive user interface. By the end of this lesson, you'll understand how to implement toggle functionality that's commonly used in dropdown menus, collapsible sections, and modal dialogs.
intro.usecase: Toggle visibility is one of the most common patterns in modern web applications, appearing in navigation menus that collapse on mobile devices, accordion sections in FAQ pages, and expandable sidebar panels in admin dashboards. You'll find this pattern in form wizards where sections show/hide based on user selections, shopping cart dropdowns that appear on hover, and notification panels that slide in from the side. Developers use toggle visibility to create cleaner interfaces by hiding secondary content until needed, such as advanced filter options in e-commerce sites or detailed project information in task management tools like Trello or Asana.
